sources.title: S. Bachmann, S. Michalakis, B. Nachtergaele, and R. Sims, Automorphic Equivalence within Gapped Phases of Quantum Lattice Systems
sources.locator: Full article PDF retrieved (31 pages); inspected: §2 Proposition 2.4, Lemma 2.6 and Corollary 2.8; §§4.1–4.4 Assumptions 4.2–4.4 and Theorems 4.5–4.8; §§5.1–5.3 Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.3; §5.5 Theorem 5.5 and Lemma 5.6.

contents.name: Proposition 2.4: differentiability of an isolated spectral projection and its transport unitary

source_review.read_extent: The complete proposition, contour-resolvent proof, and its use of the local spectral gap were inspected.
source_review.supports: The finite-dimensional Riesz-projection route and the purpose of a filtered unitary generator.
source_review.limitations: The local item supplies its own explicit integrable Fourier filter, sign convention, matrix-entry calculation, and locally fixed cluster hypothesis.

contents.name: Lemma 2.6 and Corollary 2.8: the gap filter and commutator formula for the spectral projection

source_review.read_extent: The complete filter lemma and the corollary derivation were inspected, including the Fourier convention and cross-band matrix entries.
source_review.supports: The exact spectral-gap Fourier identity and filtered derivative relation used by the local finite-volume lemma.
source_review.limitations: The local construction is re-derived with a smooth compactly supported frequency cutoff and explicitly states rapid integral tails.

contents.name: Assumptions 4.2–4.4: differentiable interactions, a uniform pathwise band gap, and a Lieb–Robinson input

source_review.read_extent: The full finite-volume assumptions and their relation to the spectral-flow construction were read.
source_review.supports: The interaction-path regularity and pathwise, volume-uniform gap conventions.
source_review.limitations: The local definition makes spectral-cluster continuity explicit because uniform set separation alone does not ensure a moving interval selects a continuous projection.

contents.name: Theorems 4.5 and 4.6: locality of spectral flow and time-dependent weighted Lieb–Robinson iteration

source_review.read_extent: The full statements and complete proof of Theorem 4.6, together with the proof route for Theorem 4.5, were inspected.
source_review.supports: The convolution iteration for time-dependent interaction paths and the resulting weighted commutator bound.
source_review.limitations: The local proof specializes to finite-dimensional spin interactions, proves the bound directly, and removes a planned finite-range commutator lemma that does not imply this weighted estimate.

contents.name: Theorem 4.8: filtered generators decompose into local shells with a uniform decaying interaction norm

source_review.read_extent: The complete shell decomposition, norm estimate, assumptions and proof of Theorem 4.8 were read.
source_review.supports: Conditional expectations, telescoping shells, and uniform decay of the filtered-generator interaction.
source_review.limitations: The local proof establishes every shell and coefficient-limit estimate for the stated finite-range specialization and every polynomial F_rho tail.

contents.name: Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.3: thermodynamic flow convergence and convergence of local generator coefficients

source_review.read_extent: The complete convergence proof and coefficient comparison were read, including the finite-volume boundary-tail estimates.
source_review.supports: Uniform convergence on local observables and stabilization of fixed local generator terms.
source_review.limitations: The local proof gives the full tail comparison, including removed interaction supports that intersect the initial observable.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5 and Lemma 5.6: automorphic equivalence of the limiting ground-state sets

source_review.read_extent: The full theorem statement and proof, and the complete state-limit comparison lemma, were read.
source_review.supports: Transport of thermodynamic limiting state sets by the limiting automorphism.
source_review.limitations: The local statement defines finite-volume band states through normalized-trace extensions and proves both inclusions; it does not assert exponential clustering.

sources.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices
sources.locator: Full lecture-notes PDF retrieved (157 pages); inspected: Chapter 3 spin-algebra and interaction setup; §4.1 Theorem 4.1.2 and its complete proof; §4.2 existence of dynamics and proof of Theorem 4.1.2.

contents.name: §4.1, Theorem 4.1.2: the Lieb–Robinson bound for local interactions

source_review.read_extent: The full theorem and complete proof were inspected, including the iteration over interaction paths and the extension to finite local supports.
source_review.supports: An independent complete treatment of the commutator-path argument and finite-range dynamics hypotheses.
source_review.limitations: Its exponential interaction norm differs from the local F_a pair norm; the local theorem proves the weighted formulation independently.

contents.name: §4.2: existence of thermodynamic dynamics from finite-volume boundary estimates

source_review.read_extent: The complete finite-volume convergence argument and boundary estimate were inspected.
source_review.supports: The local uniform-in-volume dynamics convergence used to pass fixed filtered coefficients to limits.
source_review.limitations: It does not address the filtered spectral generator or spectral-flow transport; those arguments are supplied on the A page.

contents.name: Chapter 3: finite-dimensional local spin algebras and finite-range interaction conventions

source_review.read_extent: The relevant local algebra and interaction definitions were inspected in the complete lecture-note PDF.
source_review.supports: The finite-site tensor-product setting and self-adjoint local interaction convention.
source_review.limitations: The local definition fixes the max-coordinate lattice metric and its own pair-weighted norms.

contents.name: Assumption 4.3 and Theorem 5.5: the spectral gap is required along the full interpolation path

source_review.read_extent: The complete pathwise gap assumption and its use in the thermodynamic transport theorem were inspected.
source_review.supports: The distinction between endpoint gaps and the uniform path-gap hypothesis required for transport.
source_review.limitations: The exact one-spin Hamiltonian is a local explicit counterexample calculation, not an example quoted from this article.

contents.reason: These notes prove finite-range propagation bounds but do not treat spectral-flow paths or a gap-closing example; the assigned one-spin Hamiltonian and its gap are computed directly.
